points.description: States the core fact: a static array is initialized only once (not re-initialized each time the function is called), so it persists across calls, whereas a non-static array is created/initialized again on every call.
points.partial_credit: About half: says static arrays persist/keep their values or are created once, without clearly linking to initialization or contrasting with non-static; or stated vaguely.

points.description: Ties this to function calls: the initialization happens relative to the function being called (static once across calls; non-static each call).
points.partial_credit: Mentions function calls but without clearly stating the once vs. every-call contrast.

rubric.notes: Full marks for saying a static array is initialized only once (keeps its values between function calls) while a non-static one is re-initialized each call; any wording is fine, even brief. Part marks for vague or half-right statements, e.g. only "it keeps its value" or "it lasts the whole program" without the initialization idea. No marks for unrelated points such as array size or syntax only.
